{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -p qcpu_exp
#   -A DD-23-135
#   -n 1
#   --comment "use:vtune=2022.2.0"
#   -t 0:10:00
#   --mail-type END
#   -J AVS-vtune

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  --time=10m \
  --queue=qcpu_exp \
  bash -lc '

# NOTE: Slurm -A DD-23-135 (account/project) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: Slurm --comment "use:vtune=2022.2.0" has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime (metadata only), but site tooling that keys off this comment may not work.

# NOTE: Slurm --mail-type END has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive end-of-job email.

# NOTE: Slurm job name (-J AVS-vtune) is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

cd "${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR:-$PWD}"

ml intel-compilers/2022.1.0 CMake/3.23.1-GCCcore-11.3.0 VTune/2022.2.0-intel-2021b

[ -d build_vtune ] && rm -rf build_vtune
mkdir -p build_vtune
cd build_vtune

CC=icc CXX=icpc cmake ..
make

for threads in 18 36; do
    for builder in "ref" "loop" "tree"; do
        rm -rf vtune-${builder}-${threads}
        vtune -collect threading -r vtune-${builder}-${threads} -app-working-dir . -- ./PMC --builder ${builder} -t ${threads} --grid 128 ../data/bun_zipper_res3.pts
    done
done
'
"
}
